Measure first.

- Run `pytest --durations=20 -q` to list the 20 slowest tests.
- Run `jest --verbose --runTestsByPath src/slow.test.ts` to isolate a slow file.
- Run `go test -cpuprofile cpu.out -bench . ./...` then `go tool pprof cpu.out`.
- Run `cargo test -- --nocapture` to find tests blocked by stdout or sleeps.
- Run `mvn -Dsurefire.reportFormat=plain test` to inspect per-test timing.

Parallelize the suite.

- Use `pytest -n auto --dist loadscope` with `pytest-xdist`.
- Use `jest --maxWorkers=4` or `jest --maxWorkers=50%`.
- Use `vitest --pool=threads --poolOptions.threads.maxThreads=8`.
- Use `go test -parallel 8 ./...`.
- Use `cargo test -- --test-threads=8`.
- Use `mvn -T 1C test` for Maven module parallelism.
- Use `gradle test --max-workers=8`.

Run only relevant tests.

- Use `pytest --lf` to rerun only last failures.
- Use `pytest --ff` to run last failures first.
- Use `git diff --name-only origin/main | xargs jest --findRelatedTests`.
- Use `vitest --changed origin/main`.
- Use `go test ./internal/foo/...` instead of `./...`.
- Use `cargo test -p my_crate`.
- Use `mvn -pl module-a -am test`.

Remove slow dependencies.

- Replace HTTP calls with `unittest.mock.patch("requests.get")`.
- Replace HTTP calls with `jest.mock("./api")`.
- Replace HTTP calls with `nock("https://api.example.com")`.
- Replace HTTP calls with `responses.add(responses.GET, "https://api.example.com", json={})`.
- Replace clocks with `freezegun.freeze_time("2026-01-01")`.
- Replace timers with `jest.useFakeTimers()`.
- Replace filesystem writes with `tmp_path` or `tmpfs`.
- Use `TMPDIR=/dev/shm pytest --basetemp=/dev/shm/pytest`.

Speed up database tests.

- Use `DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///:memory:` for simple tests.
- Use `pytest --reuse-db` with `pytest-django`.
- Use `pytest --nomigrations` with `pytest-django`.
- Use `@pytest.mark.django_db(transaction=False)` for rollback-based isolation.
- Use `BEGIN; ROLLBACK;` around each test.
- Use `docker run -d -e POSTGRES_DB=test -p 54

results.out:
- Use structured logs with consistent fields: `timestamp`, `level`, `service`, `trace_id`, `message`, and relevant context.
- Choose levels deliberately: `ERROR` for actionable failures, `WARN` for degraded behavior, `INFO` for lifecycle events, `DEBUG` for diagnostics.
- Include correlation IDs and send logs to a central sink with retention, search, and alerting; redact secrets and PII.

Until then, here is a standard release process:

- Tag: `git tag -a v1.2.3 -m "Release 1.2.3"`
- Push tag: `git push origin v1.2.3`
- Build artifact: `dist/app-1.2.3.tar.gz`
- Deploy target: `staging.example.com`
- Smoke test: `curl -fsS https://staging.example.com/healthz`
- Production deploy: `kubectl set image deployment/app app=registry.example.com/app:1.2.3`
- Rollback: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/app`
- Post-release check: `curl -fsS https://example.com/healthz`

Measure first. The query planner names the bottleneck; guesses don’t.

Index columns used in `WHERE`, `JOIN`, `ORDER BY`, and `GROUP BY`. Match composite index order to query predicates. Use covering indexes to avoid table lookups. Use partial indexes for hot subsets.

Avoid low-cardinality indexes unless they are selective. Every index slows writes and consumes memory. Drop unused indexes. Rebuild or analyze when stats drift.

results.out:
Technical debt is borrowed speed. You ship now. You pay later.

It is not “bad code.” It is code that works today but makes tomorrow expensive. The interest is slower changes, more bugs, riskier releases, and harder onboarding.

Treat it like money.

- If it blocks delivery, budget paydown.
- If it causes incidents, fix it.
- If nobody uses it, leave it.
- If it only feels ugly, ignore it.

Measure first. Cycle time, rework, incidents, onboarding time. Pay debt when it buys speed, reliability, or safety. Don’t pay it for pride.
